analysis.title: China: a broad weakening in October data
key_insights: China's October activity data weakened across the board and missed consensus by a wide margin. Domestic demand is weakening further, and supply indicators (industrial production, exports) are diverging from demand indicators (retail sales, investment).

Retail sales growth fell to 0.4% YoY from 1.1%, below the 0.8% consensus. A base effect from the 8-day National Day holiday in 2025 explains part of it. Jewellery sales fell 28.7% and auto sales fell 21.4%, dragging large-retailer sales by 0.6ppt and 5.6ppt respectively.

Year-to-date fixed asset investment (FAI) fell 8.1% from -7.2%. The CA-CIB calculation puts October alone at -16.1% YoY, the sharpest drop since February 2020. The decline now extends beyond property: tertiary -10.9%, manufacturing -2.9%, infrastructure -7.3% YTD. High-tech FAI held at +4.0% YTD.

Industrial production growth eased to 4.8% YoY from 5.5%, below the 5.3% consensus. Auto manufacturing fell to 0.9% from 6.7%, attributed to base effects and the coming EU import quota on Chinese EVs. High-tech manufacturing accelerated to 17.6% and IC output growth rose to 21.9%.

Property indicators worsened. Property FAI fell 21.6% YTD (34.2% YoY in October), developers' funding sources fell 28.0% YoY in October, and new home prices fell 0.2% MoM across 70 cities. YoY price declines narrowed to -2.7% for new homes and -4.3% for existing homes.

Exports grew 35.2% YoY and imports 41.6%, with the YTD trade surplus at USD1,051bn. The export value gain is mostly price inflation: IC export prices rose 143.0% while IC export volume fell 2.4%. Crude oil import growth of 41.0% came from a 62.6% price rise, with import volume down 13.3%.

CPI eased to 0.7% YoY while PPI rose to 5.7% on upstream mining, coal, oil and chemicals. The widening PPI-CPI gap points to squeezed margins for mid- and downstream firms, since upstream costs are not passing through to finished goods.

Credit stayed weak. New aggregate financing was RMB1,151bn against RMB1,448bn consensus, and RMB loans fell RMB100bn. Household loans fell RMB430bn, including a RMB156bn drop in medium and long-term loans, so the late-September mortgage subsidy shows limited effect so far. Net government bond issuance rose to RMB1,184bn.
The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1 against a 49.9 consensus, back into contraction. Construction PMI fell to 48.0 from 50.3 and services PMI to 50.0 from 50.2.

Policy support rose in October but remains incremental. RMB1.3trn of special CGBs and RMB800bn of policy bank financing tools were fully issued, and the local government issuance quota was lifted by RMB550bn. In early November the PBoC moved its policy rate to overnight, lowering the anchor for short-term money market rates by 15bp, and raised the FX deposit RRR by 2%. The report sees limited evidence of fiscal easing in the data so far.

For 2027 the report expects less supportive external demand. The AI capex cycle is set to slow, and trade tensions and US export controls may tighten after the Democratic sweep of the US midterms. The Section 301 overcapacity investigation could conclude at any time, and the Nvidia shakeup has revived US momentum for stricter chip export controls.

The report expects the 2027 growth target to stay at 4.5-5.0%, which would require more domestic demand support. It says markets and CA-CIB are not optimistic about a meaningful scale-up of fiscal expansion. Signals are due from the December Politburo meeting and the Central Economic Work Conference.

Xi and Trump are expected to meet at APEC (18-19 November, Shenzhen) and possibly at the G20 (14-15 December, Miami) to discuss extending the Busan trade truce. The truce suspends US affiliate-rule export controls and Chinese rare earth export controls. New US chip restrictions could undermine it and raise the chance of Chinese retaliation.

sector_views.rationale: Sales, starts, completions, investment and developer funding all remain in contraction, and tighter presales rules further restrain developer funding.
High-tech manufacturing output (+17.6%), high-tech FAI (+4.0% YTD) and IC exports remain the main buffer, helped by AI hardware demand and price inflation.
Auto output growth fell to 0.9% YoY, auto retail sales fell 21.4%, and EU import quotas on Chinese EVs are coming.
Upstream cost inflation is not passing through to finished goods, widening the PPI-CPI gap and pressuring corporate earnings.

risk_factors: Further weakening of domestic demand and property strain, with policy support still incremental.
Slow fiscal execution, with limited evidence so far in investment data.
Beijing's push to avoid overinvestment and excessive competition, plus government reshuffling ahead of the 21st Party Congress in October 2027.
A slowing global AI capex cycle reducing demand for Asian and Chinese hardware exports.
Tighter US chip export controls and the end of the Busan truce, raising the chance of Chinese retaliation on rare earths.
Squeezed margins for mid- and downstream firms from upstream input inflation with weak pass-through.
Export and import growth is mostly price-driven, so volume weakness could reveal softer underlying trade.
geopolitical: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet at APEC (18-19 November, Shenzhen) and possibly at the G20 (14-15 December, Miami) to discuss extending the Busan trade truce.
The Busan truce covers suspended US export controls (affiliate rule) and suspended Chinese rare earth export controls.
The Section 301 investigation on Chinese manufacturing overcapacity could conclude at any time.
The Nvidia shakeup has revived US political momentum for stricter advanced chip export controls on China.
Renewed US trade tensions and tighter export controls are possible after the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.
EU import quota restrictions on Chinese EVs are coming.
Energy price inflation tied to geopolitical uncertainty is lifting China's import bill and PPI.

tension_points.theme: China fiscal and policy easing impact
tension_points.bull_case: Fiscal and quasi-fiscal support quickened in October: RMB1.3trn special CGBs and RMB800bn policy bank tools were fully issued, the local government quota was raised by RMB550bn, and net government bond issuance reached RMB1,184bn. The PBoC and regulators eased financial conditions in early November. The report says this could in theory stabilise investment in Q4.
tension_points.bear_case: The measures remain incremental and targeted, with limited evidence in the data so far. October FAI fell 16.1% YoY by CA-CIB calculation, and execution hurdles include Beijing's limits on overinvestment and government reshuffling before the 21st Party Congress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further decline in FAI and credit data in coming prints, or no larger scale-up of fiscal expansion or demand-side measures at the December Politburo meeting and Central Economic Work Conference.

theme_stances.key_argument: October activity data surprised to the downside and points to further weakening of domestic demand amid property strain and incremental policy support.
theme_stances.evidence: surprised on the downside by a wide margin

theme_stances.key_argument: Greater policy easing efforts will be necessary to boost domestic demand materially given less supportive trade in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: greater policy efforts will be necessary to boost domestic demand more materially

theme_stances.key_argument: More restrictive US chip measures could undermine managed strategic stability and raise the probability of Chinese retaliation with its own export controls.
